key_insight: A first-principles phonon-transport model best describes thermal transport in AlGaN HEMT buffer and transition layers, yielding the most physically consistent results among three models.
engineering_relevance: More reliable layer-level thermal conductivity predictions can support thermal management and stack design in AlGaN HEMTs.
method: Compare three phonon-transport models, from a Debye approximation to DFT-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties.
Establish intrinsic transport dominated by Umklapp scattering, then add alloy, grain-boundary, and film-boundary scattering.
Fit boundary-scattering contributions to thin-film thermal conductivity measured by time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR).
evidence_signal: Comparison with TDTR measurements favors the first-principles model, although the abstract reports no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Boundary-scattering parameters fitted to specific samples may require recalibration for films with different grain structures or thicknesses.
paper_title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
